name: Abū Ḥātim Sahl ibn Muḥammad al-Sijistānī
summary: Basran lexicographer, reader and grammarian, student of al-Aṣmaʿī and al-Akhfash and teacher of al-Mubarrad and Ibn Durayd.
bio: Abū Ḥātim came from Sijistān and spent his life in Basra, learning from al-Aṣmaʿī, Abū ʿUbayda, Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī and al-Akhfash; al-Zubaydī places him in the seventh Basran generation. He was a reader of the Qurʾān and the imam of the mosque of Basra, and the sources say he knew the Qurʾān readings and rare words better than grammar.
His books on words of opposite meanings (al-Aḍdād), on the masculine and feminine and on the long-lived (al-Muʿammarūn) survive. Al-Mubarrad and Ibn Durayd were his students. He died in 255/869.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 31 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
